the specimen of the only published duduk model with a full reed parameter set; not the instrument of any recording in the library

holes 1 to 10 in order of position along the body from the reed end, which is the row order of Table 1; hole positions are printed from the body's top plane (Figure 1), tabulated here from the reed tip: the body's top plane lies 0.088 m from the tip (the 0.103 m reed of Figure 6 minus the 15 mm it fills in the body)

holes 2 and 10 (57.3 mm and 297.6 mm from the body's top plane): the two dashed circles of Figure 1. The paper says two holes are on the back and does not name them; the dashed-circle reading is the hidden-line convention (u-back-holes)

the text says the holes are all of the same size and gives no diameter; Figure 1 is a vector drawing whose ten circles all measure 9.00 mm at the stroke centreline against the drawing's own dimension lines (fit 1.04713 pt/mm over the ten hole positions, residuals at most 0.22 mm; 1.04680 pt/mm from the 354 mm body length), stroke 1.00 mm (u-hole-diameter)
Figure 6 gives a 103 mm reed of which 15 mm fills the body, so 88 mm lies outside; Figure 1 draws 89 mm (u-body-top-offset)

NOT MODELLED: the bore is a plain 12 mm duct from the reed tip. the engine's impedance check (fs-duct Bessel losses, 293.15 K, unflanged end) of the three readings of the reed interior against the Figure 7 legend peaks G-1 180.8, G 392.2 and C+1 576.8 Hz: the Figure 6 round interior (22.07 cm3) puts f1 250 to 450 cents FLAT on all eleven fingerings; the interior DERIVED from geometry (perimeter pi x D(x) of Figure 6, opening area 5.4 mm2 at the tip, minor axis linear in x: ASSUMED, 8.83 cm3) puts it 88 to 348 cents SHARP; the plain 12 mm bore through the reed region (11.65 cm3), used here, lands between -27 and +55 cents of the authors' values and carries no high-register inharmonicity (u-reed-interior)
